title: Document BMAD usage decision tree
description:
Create docs/development/bmad/when-to-use-bmad.md providing a decision guide for choosing the right BMAD approach.

## Context
Users encountering BMAD for the first time have no guidance on when to use the full roadmap-driven method vs lighter approaches. The scale-adaptive intelligence (levels 0-4) exists conceptually but there is no accessible decision tree. This is critical for adoption — without it, users either skip BMAD entirely or over-apply it to trivial changes.

## What to document
- Decision tree flowchart or table covering these paths:
  (a) Ad hoc changes with no BMAD (bug fixes, config tweaks)
  (b) Quick-spec only (small features needing a spec but not full planning)
  (c) Quick-dev (intent-in code-out for moderate changes)
  (d) Partial BMAD (skip analysis/research, start at planning or solutioning)
  (e) Full roadmap-driven BMAD (new projects, major features, multi-service work)
- How scale-adaptive levels 0-4 map to these approaches
- Criteria for each level: team size, scope, risk, compliance needs, timeline
- Examples of real scenarios and which approach fits
- How to transition: starting with quick-dev and escalating to full BMAD when complexity is discovered
- Brownfield vs greenfield considerations

## Sources to read
- src/bmad/BMAD-workflow.md for the required progression chain and conditional lanes
- BMAD-METHOD/docs/how-to/established-projects.md for upstream guidance
- bmad-overview.md for scale-adaptive intelligence description
- quick-spec and quick-dev skills for fast-path scope
close_reason: Scale-adaptive levels documented in when-to-use-bmad.md alongside the decision tree

- What Beads is and why it replaces TodoWrite/markdown task lists for BMAD delivery
- The bd command lifecycle mapped to BMAD phases:
  - bd prime: session recovery, context initialization
  - bd create: issue creation for phases, epics, stories, blockers, defects

  - bd close: marking work complete (single and batch)
  - bd sync: git synchronization at session boundaries

  - Closed during Phase Closeout
- How story issues map to implementation:

  - Claim with bd update --status in_progress
  - Close after story acceptance
- How newly discovered work is tracked:
  - Blockers, defects, carry-over work recorded with bd create
  - Not only in markdown evidence
- Workspace vs repo-local issue scoping:
  - Workspace/orchestration may have parent Beads issues
  - Child repo delivery work belongs to child repo-local issues
- Phase Closeout reconciliation:
  - Close completed phase issue
  - Create carry-over issues for deferred work
  - Run bd sync
- The Beads Control Rules from BMAD-workflow.md (7 exact rules)
